text:
Marta (Design): working through the rollback UX — proposing a compact right-side "rollback drawer" that slides over the timeline instead of a full modal. sketch + rationale: https://figma.redwood/design/rollback-drawer :link:
Jay (PM): curious about accidental rollbacks — what's the primary prevention? do we still need a blocking confirm? :thinking_face:
Alex (Design): proposal: small inline safety checkbox + a secondary confirmation step only for >50% traffic changes. default primary CTA is Cancel, primary destructive is Baja (jk) -> Rollback. microcopy options below. :pill:
Lee (Eng): from infra POV need explicit throttling + idempotent API calls. also focus management: when drawer opens, focus must move to first interactive element and trap. no background keyboard interactions.
Sam (A11y): agree on focus trap. SR should announce: "Rollback opened. Current version: v12.2. Undo available for 5 minutes." use aria-live="assertive" for that message. avoid role=dialog if we can't guarantee focus management.
Marta (Design): good call — microcopy options: 
- Option A: "Rollback to previous version. Undo available for 5 minutes."
- Option B: "Revert deployment (this can be undone for 5 minutes)."
Which reads clearer to non-technical PMs? :eyes:
Priya (Research): Option A is more direct in our tests. Also flagging motion — the drawer slide should respect prefers-reduced-motion. keep animation subtle, no pulsing on the CTA.
Ben (Data): add request-level telemetry: tag rollback events with `rollback_reason` and `traffic_before/after` so we can map rollbacks to A/B variants. also mark in timeline as `traffic_change` event.
Alex (Design): thinking about canary visibility — add a tiny pulsing badge next to the variant chip while canary < 10%. Priya: test with reduced motion. Sam: pulsing might cause vestibular issues. maybe a static yellow dot + SR text.
Lee (Eng): implementation note: prefer CSS-only slide for perf, fallback to transform/opacity, and apply `prefers-reduced-motion` static placement. here's a quick snippet:
```
.drawer { transform: translateX(100%); transition: transform 240ms ease-out; }
.prefers-reduced-motion .drawer { transition: none; transform: translateX(0); }
```
Marta (Design): for rollback confirmation flow: default focus on Cancel, keyboard Enter shouldn't activate destructive action. require explicit click on Rollback CTA or `Cmd/Ctrl+R` with warning.
Jay (PM): agree. also we should show a small inline diff of config keys and a snapshot timestamp in the drawer header to reduce confusion.
snapshot-bot: design snapshot uploaded: rollback-drawer-v2.png (hash: a3f4)
Sam (A11y): for screen readers, order should be: header (announcement), current version info, why/notes textbox, diff summary, actions. add `aria-describedby` linking CTA to digestible summary.
Marta (Design): decision checklist: 1) Drawer vs Modal -> Drawer. 2) Microcopy -> Option A. 3) Focus default -> Cancel. 4) Pulsing -> static dot. 5) Motion -> respect prefers-reduced-motion. anyone object? :thumbsup:
Jay (PM): +1 from me. let's freeze and ship an exploratory A/B to 5% of rollouts to validate.
Ben (Data): will add metrics events, can track rollback rate, time-to-undo, and errors.
Alex (Design): pushed updated frames to Figma: https://figma.redwood/design/rollback-drawer-v2 — please add final comments by EOD Friday. :tada:
Lee (Eng): will slot a spike for focus/fallback behavior in next sprint.
Marta (Design): thanks all — I'll update the spec and open a PR for copy strings. :heart:
